summary: Louis Léon Duvau was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig, and Rome, under Michel Bréal and Ferdinand de Saussure. He held posts at the Universities of Burgundy and Lille, the EPHE, and the Collège de France.

Louis Renou was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed his PhD at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Alfred Foucher. He taught at Lyon, EPHE, and the University of Paris.

Louis Trolle Hjelmslev was a linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Holger Pedersen and in Paris under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held academic posts at Aarhus University (1934–1937) and the University of Copenhagen (from 1937).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Liège, Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden. He taught Sanskrit at Liège and Leuven before serving as professor at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.
Louis-François Meunier was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Eugène Burnouf around 1845–1852 and under Michel Bréal around 1866–1869.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, studying at the Collège de France. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and was founding director and professor of Persian at INALCO from 1795 to 1824.

Louise Allison Cort is a specialist in Japanology and history and archaeology who studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College. She served as curator of ceramics at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from circa 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Louise Roche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Munich in 2023 and is attested as an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma, also studying under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, having also studied under Th. P. van Baaren, Johannes Hendrik Hospers, Fred Leemhuis, and Adam Simon van der Woude.
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Lozang Trinlae works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, earning degrees from Northeastern, Harvard, and Claremont School of Theology. He led Educational Visions and Methods (1993–2009) and was a visiting lecturer at the University of Tartu (2019–2021).

Lubor Hájek was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his PhD at Charles University under Otakar Pertold and Vincenc Lesný. He served as director of Oriental collections at the National Gallery Prague from 1952 to 1986.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from around 1978 to 1983 and held an academic post there around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa works in linguistics, Indology, and computational studies, holding posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri works in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a doctorate from the Free University of Berlin. He directed the Italian Institute for Africa and the East around 2011 and was associate professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020–2021).
Luchun Wu works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a post at Ghent University in 2025 and is attested as a PhD researcher there in 2026.

Lucia Catherine Graeme Grieve was an Indologist who studied at Wellesley College, Oxford, and Columbia University, where she earned a PhD. She taught at several female seminaries and colleges between 1883 and 1893.
